case_name: Sardul Singh with Jagtar Singh v State of Haryana
respondent:
State of Haryana
Supreme Court of India

27 September 2002
Appeal (Crl.) 634 of 2001 and Appeal (Crl.) 1191 of 2001
The Judgment was delivered by : Doraiswamy Raju, J.
1.  These two appeals are dealt with together, since they relate to the same occurrence and arise out of a common judgment of the court below. The appellant in Criminal Appeal No.634 of 2001 was accused No.1 and the third accused is appellant in Criminal Appeal No.1191 of 2001. These two along with Harvinder Singh (A2), Tikka Singh (A4) and Jaswant Singh (A5) stood charged before the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Yamuna Nagar at Jagadhri, under Sections 302, 148 and 149 of the Indian Penal Code, for having caused the death of Naresh Kumar, brother of PWs-8 and 10, and son of PW-11, at about 8 or 8.30 P.M. on 9.11.1990. Accused Nos.1 and 2 are own brothers and son of one Baldev Singh, accused No.3 is the brother's son of Baldev Singh and cousin of A1 and A2, and while A4 is the friend

statutes.act: Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: These two appeals are dealt with together, since they relate to the same occurrence and arise out of a common judgment of the court below.
The complainant party had a sugarcane crusher in the land adjoining the lands of Baldev Singh.
On 8.11.1990, A3 and two others came to the cane crusher where besides PW-8, his father; two brothers (Ramesh and Naresh) were present and abused them.
Later in the evening on that day at about 4.30/5.00 P.M., the deceased and PW-8 left for Bilaspur in a Tonga belonging to Sheo Ram...
When they were near the lands of Baldev on the link road of Ram Khera to Chouwala, the five accused, armed with lathis, raised lalkara that PW-8 and the deceased should not be allowed to go.
It was also claimed that since each were in the process of assault calling the other by names, he could identify them from their voices, being known persons.
Thereafter, PW-8, driving the Tonga brought the deceased, said to be conscious at that time to their house and both narrated the incident to their father as well as the other brother.

Earlier on the report sent by the Doctor (PW-9) at about 11.15 P.M. about the serious condition of the victim to the Police, the ASI came to the Hospital at about 1.45 A.M and recorded the statement of PW-8 and caused the case to be registered.
issues: The legal questions or points of law being debated
petitioner_arguments: It was strenuously contended for the appellant in Criminal Appeal No.634 of 2001 that the courts below including the High Court having not accepted the claim of prosecution of the recoveries made and disbelieved the version of the father (PW-11) on the alleged oral dying declaration of the deceased, there was hardly any justification for the High Court to reverse the verdict of acquittal recorded by the learned Trial Judge in respect of the said appellant.

The further contention on behalf of this appellant was that the evidence of PW-8, the brother, who claims to have accompanied the deceased in the Tonga when the incident occurred, could not, with so many glaring infirmities affecting its credibility, be the basis of conviction and that too by reversing an acquittal in favour of this appellant.
respondent_arguments: The State filed Criminal Appeal No.193-DB of 1996 questioning the acquittal of the other accused.
It was contended that the manner of consideration could hardly be said to be an objective one, sufficient and justifying to set aside the findings of the Trial Court acquitting this appellant.
court_reasoning: The statement of Krishan Gopal is consistent and inspire confidence in its truthfulness so far as the role of these two persons is concerned, i.e., Jagtar Singh and Sardul Singh.
Sardul Singh had also gone to the crusher of the complainant on the previous day and that too under the influence of liquor and had threatened.
He has a clear motive to avenge his prestige, which was in his mind because the complainant reported to the Panchayat.
The parties were known to each other intimately.
Therefore, there could not be any mistake about it.
holding: Sardul Singh is thus liable for the offence under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
